item_title: AI-infrastructure stocks fell across the board Monday, the first real equity-market reaction to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend "pace the frontier" safety essay.
mechanism: Dario Amodei's "pace the frontier" essay was published as a safety proposal — coordinated, voluntary capability-slowdown, third-party evaluators — but equity markets re-priced it as a demand signal instead: if the labs actually slow the rate of capability gains, the hyperscaler capex line under the entire AI-infrastructure chain (chips, memory, EUV tools) has less growth to justify it, so the market marked down the whole supply chain simultaneously rather than any single company's own fundamentals changing. This is the same AI-equities/long-rates transmission mechanism capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading flagged on 08-19 as showing up so far only through Japan's JGB leg (Nikkei/SoftBank/Kioxia/Arm falling together on a rates story) — today is that same "the whole chain reprices on one signal" pattern reappearing domestically, off a safety statement rather than a rate move.

scenarios.direction: The selloff is the first data point in a genuine capex-growth deceleration, not a one-day move, and hyperscalers actually trim guidance next earnings cycle.
scenarios.why: A same-day, sector-wide drop across chips, memory and EUV names — rather than one company missing its own numbers — is the shape a leading demand-growth signal would take, and it landed the same week Anthropic's own OpenAI counterpart used the identical framework to justify pulling its IPO timeline, i.e. a lab acting on the pacing logic with real capital consequences.
scenarios.precedent: The 08-19 JGB-driven Nikkei/SoftBank/Kioxia/Arm selloff read the same way in real time — rates repricing the AI-equity chain together — and proved transient within days, which argues against over-reading a single session but does not rule out this one being different.

scenarios.direction: This is a crowded-trade unwind, not a demand reassessment, and the sector recovers once positioning clears.
scenarios.why: 24/7 Wall St's own read of today's cross-section — Intel (least AI-exposed) falling hardest at ~7%, Nvidia (most AI-exposed) falling least at ~2-3% — is the opposite pattern from what a genuine AI-demand-growth scare would produce, where the most AI-exposed names should fall hardest.
scenarios.precedent: Nvidia's own OpenAI Ohio guarantee was cut from $250B to under $120B within three weeks (08-15) after investor pushback, then the broader AI trade absorbed that news and moved on within the same window — this map's own record that single risk-repricing events in this ecosystem have not so far compounded into sustained de-ratings.

context_note: No rating-agency or credit-market response has followed yet, so as of this window it is an equity-pricing event only, not (yet) a financing-cost event for the AI buildout capital-context.yaml's cross_border_credit and rate_regime readings track. Figures are premarket/early-session prices at write-up time, not confirmed closes.

item_title: The US 10-year Treasury yield closed in on 5% Monday, trading around 4.99% after touching 4.992% intraday Friday — its highest since October 2023 — as Friday's hotter-than-expected August CPI and oil-driven inflation pressure pushed September rate-hike odds to roughly 87-89%, up from 65-68% at the start of the month.
mechanism: Friday's hotter-than-expected August CPI (headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3% m/m) landed the same week Saudi Arabia's pipeline shutdown and the Hormuz standoff pushed Brent above $108 — two inflation inputs, one data-driven and one supply-driven, arriving together and pushing September rate-hike odds from 65-68% at the start of the month to roughly 87-89% now. This lands directly on capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading, which has been building toward exactly this test since the 08-24 TGA/buyback disclosure: Treasury's doubled long-end buyback ceiling (funded by a $935-950bn TGA balance, $350-400bn above the prior administration's target) was read at the time as "soft-form financial repression" escalating toward "fiscal dominance" — monetary policy subordinated to fiscal financing needs. A Fed that actually HIKES into that backdrop, rather than holding or cutting, is the scenario that would either confirm or break that framing, and Wednesday is the first real data point on which.

scenarios.direction: The Fed delivers a 25bp hike Wednesday and the long end does not retreat afterward.
scenarios.why: Would confirm the fiscal-dominance framing directly — Treasury's buyback/TGA mechanism continuing to absorb long-end supply while the Fed simultaneously tightens is the "coordinated or in tension" question capital-context.yaml posed after Warsh's 08-28 Jackson Hole speech avoided giving any reaction function at all.
scenarios.precedent: The 08-24 TGA-buyback disclosure itself: the 30-year touched a 19-year high of 5.33% intraday before pulling back only on the reporting of the mechanism, not on any policy easing — evidence the long end has already shown it can stay elevated through fiscal-side interventions alone.

scenarios.direction: The Fed holds instead, reading the oil/Iran-driven inflation component as supply-side noise rather than demand pressure, and the long end rallies on the surprise.
scenarios.why: Would be the first time this cycle a hawkish CPI/PPI run did not translate into hawkish Fed action — testing whether Warsh's committee actually treats a geopolitically-driven oil spike differently from domestically-driven inflation, a distinction his Jackson Hole speech never articulated either way.
scenarios.precedent: July's payrolls miss (-23,000 vs +83-85k consensus, published 08-07) was the sharpest data-side challenge yet to the hawkish bloc and still did not visibly soften the committee's public posture going into 09-16 — the precedent argues against a hold, but it is the closest comparable this map has.

context_note: capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading (asof 2026-08-24) is now three weeks stale against this print — it captures the TGA/buyback mechanism and the Jackson Hole speech but predates both the CPI print driving today's yield move and the Hormuz/Saudi-pipeline oil spike compounding it. This entry is the update that reading needs at its next refresh.
